newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields stronger on Moody's outlook.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields stronger on Moody's outlook.

text.p: A firm Swedish crown made yields fall and the German spread shrink four basis points to 95 on Friday.
Dealers said market strength came from U.S. credit rating agency Moody's saying the outlook for Sweden was improved.
"Moody's decision increased foreigners' desire to buy crowns and we have seen more foreigners than domestic players today," one dealer said.
The fall in yields was a result of a stronger crown and Moody's statement. "The market does not seem to be receptive to bad news," one dealer said.
Dealers said the market was now focusing on the FOMC-meeting next week even though there were no expectations of a change in interest rates.
"It always interesting to see what they will do but the market seems very convinced that there will not be a hike," one dealer said.
The six month T-bill rate fell two basis points to 4.13 percent and the ten year bond yield dropped five basis points to 6.62 percent.
The crown firmed to 4.4440 to the mark versus 4.4595 on Thursday. -- Stockholm newsroom +46-700 1017
